headline: High: shared document-processing writes and browser/network exposure create default conflict and leakage risks; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via file-based handoff.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests documents/images and can run browsers, while unstructured reads files and processes documents. If outputs are handed off through shared files or copied text, attacker-controlled document content can be reinterpreted as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertain.
conditions: IF the pair exchanges outputs through a shared filesystem or copied document text
IF untrusted documents are processed by agent_a before agent_b consumes the results
mitigations: Use a separate staging folder for untrusted inputs
Strip instructions from OCR/text outputs before passing them on
Require human review of any extracted directives
Disable automatic chaining between the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every extracted field

B_data_leakage.rationale: unstructured can read files and PaddleOCR processes documents/images; both touch document content, so a shared workspace could expose sensitive material across the pair. Neither profile shows secrets handling or strong isolation between them, but unstructured does have docker self-isolation, which reduces but does not eliminate the shared-workspace risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or workspace
IF the workspace contains sensitive documents or images
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate input directory
Remove sensitive files before running either agent
Use read-only mounts for shared source data
Verify docker isolation is enabled for unstructured
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: unstructured has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and install_packages; PaddleOCR can run browsers and has allowlisted network egress. In a shared directory or orchestrated workflow, their overlapping document-processing actions can race or overwrite artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same output directory
IF the orchestrator does not serialize file writes or lock shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Enable file locking in the orchestrator
Make intermediate outputs read-only
requires-engineering: add transactional artifact writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images, and unstructured is a document parser that can consume file-based outputs. If unstructured treats PaddleOCR output as authoritative without verification, OCR mistakes can cascade into downstream parsing or transformation errors. No explicit validation step is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF unstructured consumes PaddleOCR output as an input document
IF no verification step checks OCR confidence or source fidelity
mitigations: Add a validation step before downstream parsing
Keep source documents alongside derived text
Flag low-confidence OCR spans for review
Compare extracted text against the original file
requires-engineering: implement schema checks on handoff data

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source document processors with allowlisted egress and no declared secrets handling, so there is no documented residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is operational: if sensitive documents are routed through both tools, retention and logging policies must be aligned. The profiles do not show a direct violation, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through both agents
IF retention or logging settings differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Confirm both deployments use the same retention policy
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs
Process regulated data only in approved environments
Review privacy policy links before deployment
requires-engineering: document a shared data-handling SOP
